hints: Focus on what 2,4-DNPH actually detects, an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl, not just any C=O group.
Look closely at compound 1 streptomycin for the $H-C=O$ group at the top, that is a true aldehyde.
Check the other C=O groups in 2 and 3 to see if they are esters ($-COOR$) rather than aldehydes or ketones, then decide which list is correct.
walkthrough:
**Recall the 2,4-DNPH test**

Brady's reagent, 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, gives an orange precipitate only with aldehydes and ketones.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone} + \text{2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$
Carboxylic acids, esters, amides and acyl groups do NOT give a positive result, even though they contain $C=O$.

**Examine compound 1 streptomycin**

At the top of the structure you can see a $-CHO$ group drawn as $H$ attached to $C=O$.

That is:
$$H-C=O = \text{aldehyde}$$
So compound 1 will give the orange precipitate.

**Examine compound 2 avermectin B1b**

This is a large complex molecule, but scan all the oxygen groups carefully.

You find $-OH$ alcohol groups, $C-O-C$ ether linkages, $C=C$ alkenes, and one $O-C=O$ group which is an ester linkage in the large ring. There is no $R-CHO$ aldehyde and no $R-CO-R'$ ketone, so compound 2 is negative.

**Examine compound 3 cocaine**

Cocaine contains two carbonyl groups, one as $-CO-OCH_3$ and one as $-O-CO-R$.

Both are:
$$-COOR = \text{ester}$$
Esters do not react with 2,4-DNPH, and there is no aldehyde or ketone present, so compound 3 is negative.

**Conclude the correct combination**

Only 1 is positive, while 2 and 3 are negative.

Therefore the answer is 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean all three contain an aldehyde or ketone. Only streptomycin does, 2 and 3 contain only ester, ether and alcohol groups which do not react with 2,4-DNPH.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 are both positive. Compound 2 has an ester carbonyl ($O=C-O$) but no aldehyde ($-CHO$) or ketone ($C-CO-C$), so it is a common trap if you count any $C=O$ as positive.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 are positive but 1 is not. In fact the reverse is true, 1 has the clear aldehyde while 2 and 3 have only esters which do not give the test.
options.D: Correct. Only compound 1 contains a true aldehyde group ($H-C=O$) which forms the orange 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone precipitate. Compounds 2 and 3 contain ester carbonyls, alcohols and ethers, none of which react.
